title: Pakistan and China Hold Inaugural Boundary Joint Commission Meeting in Islamabad; India Rejects It as Having 'No Legal Basis'
detail: Pakistan and China held the inaugural meeting of a new Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission in Islamabad on September 16, 2026, co-led by Li Ya, deputy director-general of the Chinese Foreign Ministry's Department of Boundary and Ocean Affairs, and Bilal Mahmood Chaudhary, director-general (China) at Pakistan's Foreign Ministry. Islamabad described the commission — intended to cover border management, joint surveys, trade flows and people-to-people connectivity under the 1963 Sino-Pakistan Frontier Agreement — as a 'significant milestone' in bilateral ties. India's Ministry of External Affairs responded the same day through spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, rejecting the commission outright: 'There is no boundary between Pakistan and China. We reject the so-called Joint Commission, which is without any legal basis,' he said, adding that India has never recognized the 1963 'China-Pakistan Boundary Agreement' as it concerns Indian territory in Gilgit-Baltistan and Shaksgam under Pakistani or Chinese control, calling it 'illegal and invalid.' Jaiswal said 'Pakistan has no locus standi to enter into arrangements concerning Indian territory under its illegal and forcible occupation' and called on Pakistan to 'vacate from areas under its illegal and forcible occupation' rather than 'engaging in such theatrics.' Neither Pakistan nor China had responded to India's rejection as of September 16.

confidenceReason: MEA spokesperson's on-record statement reported consistently across multiple Indian Tier-2 outlets (Tribune, ANI, Deccan Herald) with matching direct quotes; the underlying Pakistan-China meeting is not independently confirmed by a Pakistani or Chinese source in this search but is not in dispute.

title: Indian Officials Say Pakistan Ramping Up Drone Activity Along LoC Amid Infiltration Pressure
detail: Indian security officials, cited in wire reporting published September 16, 2026 and syndicated across multiple outlets, said Pakistan has intensified drone activity along the Line of Control in recent weeks, deploying Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) drones and Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 platforms to map Indian troop positions ahead of possible infiltration bids and to resupply weapons to local terror networks. An Intelligence Bureau official said 'all conventional methods of infiltration have failed in the last many months,' attributing the drone escalation to that desperation. Officials noted drones have separately been used to smuggle arms, ammunition and narcotics, particularly into Punjab, and pointed to an August search operation in Rajouri triggered by a suspected Pakistani drone sighting as part of the same pattern. No specific new drone incursion incident was reported as having occurred on September 16 itself — the reporting describes an assessed trend rather than a single event.
